title: Fiber-runloop refactor and KV freshness gating API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Replace the legacy thread-intensive continuous-batcher loop with a lightweight fiber-based runloop and introduce a KV freshness gating API to reduce KV thrash and tail latency. This ticket covers the refactor of the hotpath runloop, a pluggable KV freshness policy abstraction, small dependency bumps (libaio -> 2.1, pmem-cpp 1.5.0), and a low-risk rollout plan for canarying in Dedicated clusters. The goal is to reduce p95 token latency by 10-25% under bursty traffic and cut KV pagefaults during hotkey storms.
comments: 2025-11-05: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and SRE. Alignment: keep public batcher API stable; internal scheduler pluggable interface allowed to change.

2025-11-20: Spike complete — prototype fiber-runloop (user-space fibers) shows 18% p95 improvement in microbench harness for small-sequence workloads. Prototype repo: github.com/redwood/proto-fiber-runloop (link below).
2025-12-08: Design review notes from Ravi: prefer cooperative yield points at IO-bound ops; avoid preemption to keep deterministic KV cache behavior. Action: add explicit yield in prefetch path.
2026-01-17: Dependency upgrade tested on CI: libaio 2.1 removed a regression with aio cancellation. PMem upgrade requires minor allocator shim change. Marking "needs-docs" for upgrade notes.
2026-02-10: PR 8142 opened for runloop core; reviewers (Lena, Mateo) requested clearer metrics for slot starvation and a fallback to legacy threadpool on OOMs. Added canary flag and circuit breaker.
2026-02-24: Perf run on canary-n1 (staging-dedicated) shows p99 unchanged, p95 improved 12%, KV eviction events down 28%. Observability gaps: need per-shard freshness-lag metric.

2026-03-01: Security review not required for this change but ops notified about new runtime flag. Next: finish docs, add migration test matrix, and schedule gradual rollout to US region Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Fiber runloop implemented and enabled via runtime flag without changing external API surface.
KV freshness gating API available with two built-in policies: conservative and adaptive; documented and covered by unit tests.
End-to-end performance tests demonstrate >=10% p95 reduction on small to medium sequence workloads in staging.
Canary rollout runbook created and validated with rollback path to legacy threadpool.
CI gates added: unit tests, integration tests with PMem allocator shim, and a smoke test that asserts no increased OOM rate.
Migration doc and observability dashboard updated (slot-starvation, freshness-lag, kv-evict-rate, runloop-yields-per-request).
steps: 1) Land fiber-runloop core in an opt-in flag behind runtime.canary_fiber_runloop.
2) Introduce KV freshness gating interface and two policies (conservative/adaptive) with feature flags.
3) Upgrade deps (libaio -> 2.1, pmem-cpp -> 1.5.0) in a dedicated PR and run allocator stress tests.
4) Add per-shard freshness-lag and runloop yield metrics; wire into Console dashboards.
5) Run staged perf benchmarks in staging and Dedicated canary; collect p50/p95/p99 and eviction traces.
6) Iterate on policy heuristics (thresholds, lease windows) based on perf traces and increase canary scope.
7) Full rollout with automated health checks and automatic rollback on elevated error/oom/latency signals.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: cooperative fibers reduce syscall overhead but require careful backpressure to avoid head-of-line blocking; chosen approach uses explicit yield points around IO and prefetch.
Fallback plan: runtime will expose runtime.canary_fiber_runloop=false to immediately revert to legacy threadpool. Ops runbook added.
Longer-term: consider exposing KV policy knobs per-tenant for Dedicated customers after stable rollout.
